user_goal: Find a Shanghai→Tokyo flight for this Friday; meanwhile get first-timer advice on where to stay and how to get from the airport.

turns.text: Hey, could you check flights from Shanghai to Tokyo for this Friday?
While that's running... it's my first time in Tokyo. Which area should I stay in if I want to get around by subway easily?
Ha, Shinjuku sounds fun. I've always wanted to see the Shibuya crossing at night, though my friend says it's overrated.
Oh, and how do I get from the airport into the city? Is there a train, or should I just grab a taxi?
Great, thanks. I'll think about which one to book tonight.

goals.summary: One flight search Shanghai→Tokyo on 2026-03-20; cheapest is Spring Airlines 9C8515 at $189 (lands Narita); results delivered once.

checkpoints.must: Recommend one or more well-connected areas (e.g. Shinjuku, Tokyo Station/Marunouchi, Shibuya, Ueno) with a reason tied to subway/rail access. May mention the flight search is still running.
checkpoints.must_not: Only say it is still searching; claim flight results that have not arrived.

checkpoints.must: Respond briefly and naturally to the chit-chat (e.g. a light opinion on Shibuya crossing).
checkpoints.must_not: Start a hotel search or change the flight search; deliver a long unrelated monologue.

checkpoints.must: Explain airport-to-city options (Keikyu / Tokyo Monorail from Haneda, Narita Express / Skyliner from Narita, limousine bus, taxi is expensive). Ideally notes that the cheapest flight lands at Narita. The flight result arrives while the user asks this: answer first, deliver results right after.
checkpoints.must_not: Ignore the question to only read out flight results.

failure_conditions: Answers u2/u4 only with 'still searching' or defers them until results arrive.
Reports a flight not on 2026-03-20 or not from Shanghai (e.g. $159 on Saturday, $150 from Beijing).
Starts an unrequested hotel search or modifies the search after chit-chat.
Never reports flight results, or reports them repeatedly without being asked.
Cuts across the user's airport question by reading results before answering it.
